findings.title: Non-deterministic provider selection when order values are equal
findings.body: detectProvider sorts providers by order descending and picks the first. If two or more providers have the same order (e.g., DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all have order 200), the selection depends on the unspecified iteration order of ServiceLoader. Previously, the code threw an IllegalStateException when multiple providers were found, preventing this ambiguity. Now, a misconfigured classpath could silently select the wrong crypto provider, leading to runtime failures or security issues (e.g., using non-FIPS provider in a FIPS-required environment). The selection should either require unique order values or handle ties explicitly (e.g., throw if multiple providers share the highest order).

findings.title: Dead code: encoders created and discarded
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create new ASN1Encoder instances, write BigInteger values to them, and discard the results. This is dead code and should be removed. It does not affect correctness but is confusing and wasteful.

findings.title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 sequences are silently accepted as empty
findings.body: readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (tag 0x80). readSequence() then loops while length > 0, so a sequence with indefinite length will yield an empty list without consuming any content. This is incorrect and can lead to parsing failures or silent misinterpretation of input. For DER-encoded ECDSA signatures (which must be definite-length), the decoder should throw an IOException or support indefinite-length properly.

findings.title: Length validation uses total buffer size instead of remaining bytes
findings.body: The check `if (length >= limit)` compares the declared length against the total byte array length, not against the number of bytes remaining to be read. If a length is smaller than the total buffer but larger than the remaining unread bytes, the check passes and the subsequent read will eventually hit EOF and throw IOException. While not a security issue, the validation is not accurate and may allow malformed input to be processed further than necessary.

findings.title: Test uses a single EC key pair for all three curves
findings.body: The test generates one KeyPair using the default EC curve (likely secp256r1) and uses it to sign data for ES256, ES384, and ES512. The signature length passed to asn1derToConcatenatedRS/concatenatedRSToASN1DER depends on the curve, but the actual key does not match the algorithm's curve. The test only verifies round-trip conversion, which may pass even if the conversion is incorrect for certain curves (e.g., handling of leading zeros). The test should generate a proper key pair for each algorithm to ensure the conversion functions work correctly across different key sizes.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: The method getBouncyCastleProvider returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is typically the SUN or SunJCE provider, not BouncyCastle. Other CryptoProvider implementations return an actual BouncyCastle provider. This may mislead callers that expect BC-specific behavior or cause unexpected failures if BC algorithms are requested. The method name is misleading and the implementation may not fulfill the contract.
